summary: Cross-project contracts, phase 3: the gate bites. `phasekit-contracts.py check` refuses when a declared contract is unobtainable (exit 3 — no provider, or the provider does not offer it) and when the vendored copy has drifted from the mounted one (exit 4 — byte-exact tree comparison over sha256 digests). `refresh` is the one command that fixes drift, and every drift message names it verbatim. run-until-done.sh calls the gate from inside run_verify_gate, before the VERIFY_SKIP bypass, and both gates now share one record_verify_failure() writer so the artifact, the attempts counter and the VERIFY_MAX_ATTEMPTS breaker behave identically whichever gate refused.
decision_memo: foundry-meta/KICKOFF-phasekit-v070-contracts.md phase 3; enforcement per DESIGN-cross-project-contracts.md fork C and the 'Amended 2026-08-16 (later)' lockfile pattern
suggested_commit_message: v0.7.0 phase 3: the contracts gate — vendored == mounted, or refuse
reviewer_notes: The gate lives in a phasekit-owned script invoked by the loop, NOT only in the project-owned scripts/phasekit-verify.sh. A repo that can edit away the check that polices it is not policed — the same principle that puts the secret-lint allowlist on the operator side of the deploy boundary.

Scoping decision: the contracts gate runs BEFORE the VERIFY_SKIP bypass. VERIFY_SKIP is the routine per-iteration hatch for red TDD commits and docs-only phases; if it also switched off contract authenticity, the gate would be off exactly when a red gate is applying the pressure to cheat. PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_SKIP=1 is a separate, loud, operator-only hatch. Both halves are proven end-to-end against the real loop, not just grepped.

Distinct exit codes because the two failures need different human actions: DRIFT (4) is fixed by one command in this repo; UNOBTAINABLE (3) is fixed somewhere else entirely (the provider, or the project registry). Collapsing them would send people to the wrong place.

Refusal messages state the boundary rather than leaving it to be discovered: they name PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_DIR for standalone use and say explicitly that the ordinary test suite does NOT need a provider. The 'the command named by the failure message is the one that works' test parses the command out of the message and runs it, so the two cannot drift apart.

Comparison recipe is content-only (sha256 over bytes, recursive): mtimes, ownership and directory order are ignored because a bind mount and a git checkout will never agree on those, and a pin that fires on them is noise that teaches people to bypass the gate. Non-regular files are a hard error rather than a skip — a skipped symlink is a hole an inauthentic copy could hide in.

refresh replaces rather than merges, so a file the producer deleted disappears here too; otherwise the vendored copy slowly becomes a superset nobody notices. It stays manual by design — auto-refresh at dispatch would dirty the tree and trip clean-tree guards.
contracts.yaml present but the checker missing (a stale vendored scripts/ dir) WARNs loudly rather than passing quietly: a declaration nobody checks is the failure this release exists to prevent.

The kickoff's ownership trap is now pinned by test: contracts.yaml is registered nowhere, and a real enrich-then-upgrade cycle is asserted to leave the file byte-identical while still installing the checker that reads it.

deferred_items.description: Session-prompt awareness (a mount nobody is told about goes unread), stack-profile seeding of the consumer check, docs/CONTRACTS.md + CONTAINERIZATION + QUALITY_GATES + README, capability registration review, tag and push v0.7.0.

commands_run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'  -> 232 tests OK
manual smoke: drift / no-provider / refresh-then-pass messages read correctly in a scratch consumer repo
verification.acceptance_criteria_met: a deliberately edited vendored copy fails the gate; a deliberately stale one fails with the exact refresh command in the message; a repo declaring nothing is entirely unaffected (the loop never even mentions contracts)
